title: The Fortress
novel: Robin asked Barney to sell his bachelor pad. The apartment was filled with [[memorabilia|memorabilia]] from Barney's single days. It had hidden [[cameras|camera]], a special bed, and many other [[questionable|questionable]] features. Robin felt uncomfortable in the apartment and wanted a fresh start. She said they could not start their married life in a place full of Barney's old [[schemes|scheme]]. Barney was [[reluctant|reluctant]] to give up his apartment. He had many [[memories|memory]] there and felt attached to the place. He told Robin that the apartment was a part of who he was. Robin [[understood|understand]] but said they needed a home that belonged to both of them. Meanwhile, Lily's job as an art [[consultant|consultant]] put a strain on her relationship with Marshall. She was traveling a lot for work and was often away from home. Marshall had to take care of Marvin by himself while Lily was away. He was [[exhausted|exhaust]] and felt [[overwhelmed|overwhelm]] by the responsibility. He told Lily that he needed more help at home. Lily felt [[guilty|guilty]] about being away so much. She loved her job but also loved her family. They had a difficult conversation about how to [[balance|balance]] work and family. Marshall suggested that Lily cut back on her travel, but Lily was afraid of losing her job. They eventually [[compromised|compromise]] and found a way to make things work. Barney finally agreed to sell his apartment after Robin helped him see that their future together was more important than his past.

memory.en: things you remember from the past
